planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring in cool, moist, well-drained soil in partial shade sheltered from hot afternoon sun and drying wind.

directions: Cordyline indivisa, the mountain cabbage tree or blue dracaena, is a strikingly different species from the common ti plant, forming a single unbranched trunk topped by a dense rosette of broad, blue-green sword leaves several feet long with a bold red-orange midrib. Native to cool, misty mountain forests in New Zealand, it is more cold-hardy than Cordyline australis but far less heat-tolerant, struggling through prolonged humid heat and preferring filtered light with cool nights and consistently moist, well-drained soil. Grow it in part shade with shelter from harsh afternoon sun and drying wind, and mulch the root zone to keep it cool through summer. In marginal zones, container culture lets the plant be moved to a sheltered spot for winter, since it resents both hard freezes and extended heat stress.
sources: North Carolina State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

planting.note: Plant after the last frost in humus-rich, well-drained soil; unlike most cordylines, it tolerates anything from full sun to deep shade.

directions: Cordyline stricta, the narrow-leaved palm lily, is an Australian rainforest-margin species distinct from the tropical ti plant, forming dense clumping canes clothed in slender, dark green, toothed-edged leaves only an inch or two wide and up to twenty inches long. Unlike sun-loving cabbage palms, it is remarkably shade tolerant, thriving anywhere from full sun to deep shade beneath a tree canopy, and produces showy sprays of lavender-mauve flowers followed by glossy black berries, the only Australian cordyline with black fruit. Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil and water regularly while establishing; established clumps tolerate moderate drought and make an effective narrow screen or shaded understory accent. Thin older canes at the base occasionally to control height and keep the clump full and dense.
sources: PlantNET - New South Wales Flora Online
North Carolina State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring in well-drained soil in full sun, sheltered from harsh winter wind.

directions: Torbay Dazzler is a variegated cabbage palm selection prized for its cream-and-green striped, sword-shaped leaves with an occasional soft red flush along the midrib, giving a brighter, more colorful presence than the plain green species. It develops the same palm-like silhouette as straight Cordyline australis, starting as a single leafy tuft on a slender stem and eventually branching into multiple crowns as it matures over many years, with fragrant creamy flower panicles appearing on well-established specimens in summer. Grow it in full sun in well-drained soil sheltered from harsh winter wind, since the variegated foliage is somewhat more cold-sensitive than solid green forms and benefits from protection or container culture at the cooler edge of its range. It is notably salt- and drought-tolerant once established, making it a strong choice for coastal and xeriscape plantings.

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade for the deepest purple color.

directions: Purple Tower is a dark-leaved cabbage palm selection grown for its narrow, plum-purple to burgundy sword leaves that hold their rich color better in strong light than many other purple cordyline selections. It forms an upright, single-trunked accent while young, eventually thickening into a small palm-like tree, and mature plants produce dense clusters of small creamy-white, fragrant flowers in summer, though container specimens rarely bloom. Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; it tolerates coastal salt spray and brief drought once established but appreciates regular water during the first growing season. In regions with winter lows below the low 20s Fahrenheit, grow it in a container that can be moved to shelter, since a hard freeze will kill the crown.

planting.note: Transplant after the last frost into fertile, well-drained soil in partial shade to bright filtered light; suits containers as well as garden beds.

directions: Baby Doll is a compact ti plant selection that stays notably smaller and denser than most Cordyline fruticosa cultivars, forming an upright, columnar clump of broad, olive-and-moss green leaves edged in soft pink, with new growth emerging in deep chocolate-mahogany tones that mature toward green. Its dwarf three-to-four-foot habit makes it especially well suited to patio containers, poolside plantings, and smaller garden beds where full-size ti plants would quickly outgrow the space. Grow it in fertile, well-drained soil in partial shade to bright filtered light, keeping humidity high and the root zone evenly moist, since it is sensitive to temperatures below 50 degrees Fahrenheit. Bring container plants indoors well before frost, and use a humidifier or pebble tray to help it thrive as a houseplant through winter.
sources: North Carolina State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

planting.note: Plant after the last frost in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade with bright, filtered light for the strongest pink coloring.

directions: Candy Cane is a boldly striped ti plant cultivar whose green leaves are streaked with cream and edged in vivid hot pink, creating a barber-pole pattern of color that stands out even among the many variegated cordyline selections. Its preference for dappled light sets it apart from sun-loving landscape ti plants, coloring up best with bright, filtered light rather than direct hot sun, which can scorch the thinner variegated leaf tissue. Grow it in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade, keeping the root zone consistently moist through the growing season and reducing water somewhat in winter. As with other Cordyline fruticosa cultivars, protect it from any frost and move container specimens indoors or to a sheltered spot before temperatures drop into the 40s.
sources: North Carolina State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox
